OK, so it seems obvious that there is significant voter fraud in a few states at least. You'll hear lots of arguing from "data scientists" and other people who lack imagination and want to argue against a straw man.

Step 1: Register to vote. Usually registering requires some form of proof that you exist or have an ID. Certain states have gone out of their way to make this easy for illegal immigrants, others have not. Now, that doesn't mean you can't register dead people or people who don't really live in the area (if the registration board doesn't check against a list). These are small beans - the real fun is in the people who DON'T REGISTER TO VOTE. You simply register them yourself and can safely assume they won't be voting as they're not even aware of the fact that they're registered or where. I think this is a significant area of fraud with potential to be uncovered.

Step 2: Actually vote. On voting day, if no ID is required, you can vote under someone else's name.

So, let's say you're a large political organization with a so-called "Get out the vote" operation. This consists of a LOT of data on who actually votes, as in their actual names, demographics, etc. This is how they figure out who to call and visit and help vote to drive turn-out on election day. They have enormous volumes of data on individual voters. One of these pieces of data is "Who is registered, but doesn't vote?" If you have a list of those names and their polling places, and no requirement to identify yourself at a polling place beyond giving a name, well golly-gee you can send whomever you want to vote there using their name without much concern.

Now, this is technically a crime, so you need to trust the people doing it. Get a crew together of people you have leverage over, like maybe they're illegal immigrants and you can deport their ass if they talk. Round them up into groups and drive them around to various polling places voting in the name of those who don't vote. The later in the day, the easier, because you can have your friends inside the polling places tell you which names have not voted!

Next, you make sure the people doing the counting are on your side. This is easy, you get the same people who used to run voting crews with you and get them to volunteer at polling places. These people are usually hardcore party loyalists and it's safe to say that many are willing to do what it takes to ensure their side wins. These people have several options depending on the type of voting system used at their polling place. Here are a few ways they can influence vote totals:

1 - Limit voting by creating long lines. You can do this by having too few polling places, having too few polling stations, having the digital stations "break" at the last minute, being slow to hand out ballots, find names, etc. This is actually a favorite technique of Republicans historically.

2 - Remove people's names from the registered voter list. Both parties do this, Republicans notoriously in Florida in 2000 election and Democrats famously in New York City during the Sanders/Clinton primary. If they're not registered, they can't vote! There are several techniques using "caging lists" to guess how a group of people will vote, then block as many as possible and figure the numbers will work in your favor.

3 - Stuff the registered voter lists. This is a Democratic party specialty - this is why they try to repeal laws that block felons from voting in some states and make it as easy as possible to register (ie removing barriers such as checks to make sure you're valid, not registered in another district, etc).

4 - Damage ballots. An experienced poll worker can guess reasonably well how a person is going to vote - not 100% but if they target 100 people and they get 70 of them correct, that''s a pretty huge swing to their advantage. Once a ballot is submitted it often goes into a scanner, or is entered into a box for counting later. At either stage it's possible to cause the ballot to be flagged incorrectly. They can also simply swap out the ballot you gave them with one they filled out on their own and throw yours in the trash.

5 - Stuffing the ballot box. The most classic election fraud technique involves simply having the poll workers enter a bunch of extra ballots into the machine, or as in the case of Detroit this year, simply scan the ones you have twice! In a really sloppy system where nobody checks the numbers carefully (VERY common) you can add as many votes as you want without much trouble. If your party controls the governing agencies and has your back, there's no risk. This is probably the most common type of election fraud by poll workers.

6 - Fuck up the count. This works differently in places but the general theme is the same - polling place submit their individual vote data to a central/regional tabulation center. This center can make "errors" or discard things through a variety of techniques specific to their process. In a system like ours where these things are very rarely audited, this is also pretty easy to do.

7 - Hack the electronic tabulators. This is the most nefarious and likely significant factor in this era. Voting machines using closed-source software have ostensibly been "audited" by government officials but we all know that's no assurance at all. Numerous instances have been noted of voting machines being "poorly calibrated" and mistaking votes right in front of the voter! If there is no receipt/paper trail, which many Dem and Repub politicians vehemently oppose, it's impossible to measure this. Further, each individual voting machine is tabulating its votes throughout the day. If the software is written in such a way as to alter that, it's basically impossible for the public to check. Next, you can code the central "tabulator" to skim votes from polling places in such a way as to alter the vote. There is a lot of statistical analysis out there for various elections including this years Sanders/Clinton primary showing very likely anomalies. The general feeling is that using electronic tabulation methods with receipts/paper ballots you can only steal around 3.5% before it becomes obvious on a statistical analysis.

As you can see, there are **MANY **opportunities in the voting process for fraud. This has been known forever and there are methods available and sometimes implemented to address each of this points. The US voting system is managed by each state, and then further by each county, and ultimately is entirely localized. Enforcement varies, corruption is inevitable (particularly in one-party dominant areas like many large cities), and elected officials who may have a stake in the process or guilt are in charge of making sure it works correctly. No reasonable person with a lick of sense about American culture can honestly believe that our elections are not rife with fraud of various sorts. The traditional view has been that it's "part of the game" and the two party monopoly looks the other way because ultimately they both engage in these sorts of practices as a means of maintaining control, particularly in their own strongholds. If Dems don't make a fuss when GOP regions do shady stuff and likewise for the GOP in Dem regions, well that's just a gentlemanly agreement.

A proper audit and investigation will inevitably turn up problems. The biggest potential for turning an election with the lowest risk is in my opinion having crews of people vote multiple times in multiple places with no checks to ensure they're who they say they are and have not voted elsewhere.
